summary: Resolved the open gap on the removed-member investigation by reading the library's own contract instead of inferring intent. doc.go's MsgProp description states that a leader appends the entries it receives and broadcasts them, a candidate drops them, and a follower stores them with the sender's ID to forward onward - with no eligibility condition anywhere - and no statement in doc.go, node.go or README assigns proposer authorization to the library; the facade's only membership-based filtering is for response messages from ids absent from Progress. That answers the gap in favour of caller-owned authorization, so the suspicion is refuted as a library defect and the interpretation moves to explained with the gap marked resolved. Everything measured earlier is retained as facts: the facade re-enables its proposal channel on any observed leader change regardless of membership, the removal branch's own comment concedes the logic is unsound, stepFollower forwards MsgProp without a membership test, and the probe showed a leader accepting a MsgProp from a just-removed id and appending one entry. One caller-facing caveat is kept without being called a defect: an application that infers membership from Propose failing will be misled after the next leader change. No severity or safety consequence is claimed, and voter eligibility and commit quorums are unaffected.
